name: Reserve Coffee
tagline: A roastery café on Makhtumkuli: rare lots, tastings and roasting in front of you

listing.description: A site for a premium café, roastery or wine bar: dark copper, a rotating seal, tasting flights and a roast curve that draws itself as you scroll.

seo.title: Reserve Coffee — roastery and coffee tastings in Tashkent
seo.description: A café with its own roaster at 3 Makhtumkuli St: rare lots from Ethiopia, Panama and Colombia, tasting flights and brewing workshops. Daily 9:00–23:00.
seo.answer: Reserve Coffee is a roastery café at 3 Makhtumkuli St in Tashkent, open daily 9:00–23:00. Beans are roasted on site in small batches. A three-lot tasting flight costs 95,000 UZS, a pour-over workshop 290,000 UZS and a private tasting for up to 8 people 1,400,000 UZS.

sections.title: Coffee roasted in front of you
sections.subtitle: A copper roaster in the middle of the room, rare lots that arrive once a season and a barista who will tell you why this cup smells of jasmine.

sections.label: The roastery
sections.title: Twelve minutes that decide the taste
sections.text: We bring in green beans in small lots directly from importers and roast them right here in the room, fifteen kilos at a time. Every batch is cupped before it reaches a cup or a bag. That is why the menu changes: some coffees end for good, others appear for a single season.

items.name: Espresso of the day
items.text: ask the barista — it changes daily

items.name: Private tasting

A batch roasted in front of you

items.title: Charge
items.text: Green beans drop into a drum heated to 200 °C.

items.title: Drying
items.text: For the first four minutes the beans lose moisture and turn yellow.

items.title: First crack
items.text: Around minute nine the beans crack and the flavour starts to develop.

items.title: Development
items.text: Two or three minutes decide whether the coffee turns floral or chocolatey.

items.title: Drop
items.text: The beans cool on the tray in four minutes and rest for three days.

items.quote: For the first time I understood that coffee can smell of peach without any syrup.
items.author: Kamila

items.quote: We celebrated our company’s anniversary here — the barista roasted a batch right in front of us.
items.author: Farhod

items.quote: Since the workshop my coffee at home beats what I used to get in any café.
items.author: Anna

sections.label: The room
sections.title: Copper, wood and the smell of roasting

items.caption: The roaster in the middle of the room

items.q: Do I need to book a tasting flight?
items.a: No, you can order a flight any time. Booking is only needed for cupping, workshops and private tastings.
Thursdays from 10:00 to 14:00 — come and watch.

items.q: Can I buy beans to take home?
items.a: Yes, 250 g bags from 140,000 UZS. We’ll grind them for your brewer.

items.q: Is the room good for business meetings?
items.a: Yes, there is a separate table for eight by the window — book it in advance.

sections.label: Contact
sections.title: Come for a tasting
sections.text: 3 Makhtumkuli — five minutes from Hamid Olimjon metro. We roast on Thursdays from 10:00.
